title: Grade 8 Science — Thu, Jun 26
description: Force and Pressure — Day 4 of 5: Atmospheric pressure, fluids, buoyancy
subject: science

questions.question: Buoyancy (upthrust) is:
options: The weight of an object in air
The upward force exerted by a fluid on any object submerged in it — opposing gravity, it makes objects feel lighter
The downward force of a fluid
The friction between fluid and object
questions.explanation: Buoyancy = upward push from fluid on submerged object. Why: fluid pressure increases with depth → pressure on bottom face > top face → net upward force. This force = weight of fluid displaced (Archimedes' Principle). Ships float, swimmers float — all due to buoyancy.

questions.question: Archimedes' Principle states:
options: Pressure = Force/Area
An object in a fluid experiences upthrust equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the object
Fluids exert pressure in all directions
Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
questions.explanation: Archimedes' Principle: Upthrust (buoyant force) = Weight of fluid displaced. If you submerge a 1,000 cm³ object in water, it displaces 1,000 cm³ of water → upthrust = weight of 1,000 cm³ of water (= 1 kg × 10 = 10 N). This explains floating, sinking, submarines.

questions.question: An object floats when:
options: Its weight > buoyant force (sinks)
Its weight = buoyant force — the object displaces exactly its own weight in fluid
Its weight < buoyant force — object rides high on surface
Its density equals 1 g/cm³
questions.explanation: Float condition: Weight = Buoyant force. This happens when the object's average density ≤ fluid density. A hollow steel ship floats because its average density (steel + air inside) < water density. Objects sink when weight > buoyancy (density > fluid density).

questions.question: Why does an iron needle sink in water but an iron ship floats?
options: The ship is made of lighter iron
The ship's hollow structure means its average density (iron + air) < water density — it displaces more water; needle is solid iron with density > water
Ships have special coating
Size alone determines floating
questions.explanation: Iron density (7,900 kg/m³) > water (1,000 kg/m³) → solid iron sinks. But a ship is hollow — its total volume includes lots of air → average density < water density → floats. The ship displaces a weight of water equal to its total weight. Density of material ≠ average density of object.

questions.question: Dead Sea (salt water, density ~1,240 kg/m³) is famous because people float very easily. Why?
options: The Dead Sea is very shallow
Higher density of salt water → greater buoyant force for same volume displaced → body floats effortlessly without swimming
The Dead Sea has special minerals that create magic
Wind pushes people up in the Dead Sea
questions.explanation: Buoyancy = weight of fluid displaced = volume × fluid density × g. Saltwater denser than freshwater → more upthrust for same submerged volume → body floats higher and more easily. The Dead Sea is so salty (~10× normal sea salinity) that the upthrust exceeds body weight easily — you can't sink.

questions.question: A submarine submerges by:
options: Adding more engine power
Filling ballast tanks with water to increase average density > seawater — upthrust < weight → submarine sinks; pumps water out to rise
Reducing speed to sink
Using propellers to go down
questions.explanation: Submarine: ballast tanks. Surface: tanks full of air → average density < water → floats. Submerge: flood tanks with water → average density > water → sinks. Rise: pump water out → average density < water → rises. This is pure buoyancy control — no engine power needed to change depth.

questions.question: A block of wood in water: weight = 20 N, buoyant force = 20 N. What happens?
options: Sinks completely
Floats completely submerged at surface
Floats with part above water surface (weight = buoyant force when partially submerged)
Shoots up above water
questions.explanation: Weight = Buoyant force = 20 N → floating. For a wood block (density < water), equilibrium is reached when only part is submerged (displacing just enough water to equal its weight). If wood density = 0.6 g/cm³ → 60% submerged, 40% above water.

questions.question: Hot air balloons float in air because:
options: Hot air is lighter than air
Heating the air inside the balloon makes it expand → density of hot air inside < density of cool outside air → buoyancy of surrounding cooler air lifts the balloon
The balloon material repels gravity
Strong fans push the balloon up
questions.explanation: Buoyancy applies to gases too! Hot air expands → same volume but fewer molecules → lower density than surrounding cool air. The balloon displaces cool air; upthrust (weight of displaced cool air) > weight of (balloon + hot air) → net upward force → balloon rises. Same principle as convection currents.

questions.question: Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude because:
options: The sky is colder at higher altitudes
At higher altitude, there is less air above → less air weight pressing down → less pressure
Gravity decreases linearly with altitude
Higher altitude has more clouds blocking pressure
questions.explanation: Atmospheric pressure = weight of air column above. At sea level: full column of atmosphere above. At 5 km: only the air above 5 km presses → less pressure. At Mt. Everest (8.8 km): pressure ≈ 1/3 of sea level. Less O₂ available per breath → mountaineers need supplemental oxygen.

questions.question: Pascal's Law: Pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally to all parts. Which device uses this?
options: Thermometer
Hydraulic brake — foot presses brake pedal (small piston/area); pressure transmitted through brake fluid equally; large piston at brake pad applies greater force to disc
Barometer
Ammeter
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake: F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂ (pressure transmitted unchanged). Small foot force on small piston creates same pressure in fluid → large piston at wheel has large area → applies much larger force on brake pad → car stops. Pascal's Law is the basis of all hydraulic systems.

questions.question: Upthrust on an object is GREATEST when:
options: The object has the greatest weight
The object displaces the greatest volume of fluid — upthrust = ρ×V×g (density of fluid × volume displaced × g)
The object is lightest
The fluid temperature is highest
questions.explanation: Upthrust = ρ_fluid × V_displaced × g. Two factors: (1) denser fluid → more upthrust (salt water > fresh water for same volume). (2) Greater volume submerged → more upthrust. Object weight determines sink/float but not the upthrust directly. Greater volume displaced = greater upthrust.

questions.question: Why does an egg sink in fresh water but float in highly salted water?
options: Salt changes the egg
Salt water has higher density → greater buoyant force for same volume. Egg density (≈1.03 g/cm³) > fresh water (1 g/cm³) → sinks. Salt water density can exceed 1.03 → upthrust > egg weight → floats
Fresh water is colder
Salt reacts with egg shell
questions.explanation: Egg density ≈ 1.03 g/cm³. Fresh water density = 1.00 g/cm³ < egg → sinks. Salt water: add enough salt → density > 1.03 → upthrust > egg weight → floats. This is a simple density demonstration — add salt until egg floats. Classic experiment in school labs.

questions.question: When you lift a heavy stone in water, it feels lighter than in air. The apparent weight loss =
options: The friction of water on the stone
The weight of water displaced by the stone (= upthrust / buoyant force) — Archimedes demonstrated this by measuring the overflow
The temperature difference between water and air
The chemical reaction between stone and water
questions.explanation: Apparent weight in water = actual weight − upthrust. Upthrust = weight of water displaced. Archimedes proved this: overflow water collected when object submerged; weight of overflow = buoyant force experienced. The stone 'loses' weight equal to the displaced water's weight.

questions.question: Why do fish have swim bladders?
options: To breathe oxygen
Swim bladder filled with gas lets fish change its volume → average density changes → fish can hover at different depths without constantly swimming
To digest food
To communicate with other fish
questions.explanation: Swim bladder = internal gas sac in fish. By absorbing or releasing gas, fish changes total volume (and thus average density) to match water density at desired depth → neutral buoyancy → hovers effortlessly. Submarines use the same principle with ballast tanks. Natural application of Archimedes' principle.

questions.question: A ship moves from a river (fresh water) to the sea (salt water). What happens to the ship's waterline?
options: Ship sinks deeper in the sea
Ship rises higher in the sea — saltwater is denser, so less volume needs to be displaced to generate the same upthrust equal to the ship's weight
Nothing changes
Ship sinks in salt water
questions.explanation: Upthrust = ρ×V×g must equal ship's weight. Salt water: higher ρ → less V needed to displace for same upthrust → ship displaces less volume → rises higher. Plimsoll line on ships marks maximum safe loading level for different water types (fresh water / salt water / tropical salt water).
